name: Accessory
simple: An Accessory is an item a character wears, like a hat, hair, glasses, wings or a backpack. It holds a part named Handle with an Attachment inside. When added to a character, the Attachment snaps onto the matching Attachment on the body, like HatAttachment on the head.
analogy: An Accessory is like a clip-on badge. The badge has a clip (the Attachment in its Handle), and the shirt has a matching spot (an Attachment on the body with the same name). Clip them together and it stays put.
whenToUse: Give a character a hat, sword on the back, wings, or other wearable item.
Check what kind of item something is (AccessoryType).
Remove or change what players are wearing.
where: Inside a character Model when worn. Keep spare ones in ServerStorage and add them with `humanoid:AddAccessory(accessory)` from a server Script. Accessory inherits from Accoutrement.

terms.Handle: The Part inside the Accessory that you see. It's what gets attached to the body.
terms.Attachment: An invisible point on a part. The accessory's Attachment and the body's Attachment with the same name are joined together.
terms.weld: A connection that glues two parts together so they move as one.
terms.layered clothing: 3D clothes like jackets that wrap around the body. They use a WrapLayer inside the Handle.
terms.Enum.AccessoryType: The list of accessory kinds, like Hat, Hair, Face, Neck, Shoulder, Front, Back, Waist, and clothing types like Jacket.
terms.R6 / R15: The two kinds of Roblox character bodies (6 parts or 15 parts). Accessories work on both.

examples.title: Give every player a hat when they spawn
examples.place: Script in ServerScriptService (put an Accessory named PartyHat in ServerStorage)
examples.code:
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ServerStorage = game:GetService("ServerStorage")
local hatTemplate = ServerStorage:WaitForChild("PartyHat")

Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
    player.CharacterAppearanceLoaded:Connect(function(character)
        local humanoid = character:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
        if humanoid then
            local hat = hatTemplate:Clone()
            humanoid:AddAccessory(hat) -- snaps HatAttachment to the head
        end
    end)
end)
explain: The PartyHat Accessory must have a Part named Handle, and inside the Handle an Attachment named HatAttachment.
AddAccessory looks for an Attachment on the body with the same name (the head has HatAttachment) and welds them together.
We wait for CharacterAppearanceLoaded so the player's own items are already on.
This runs on the server so everyone sees the hat.

examples.title: List what a character is wearing
examples.code:
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
    player.CharacterAppearanceLoaded:Connect(function(character)
        local humanoid = character:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
        for _, accessory in humanoid:GetAccessories() do
            print(accessory.Name .. " is a " .. accessory.AccessoryType.Name)
        end
    end)
end)
explain: GetAccessories returns every Accessory on the character.
AccessoryType tells you what kind it is, like Hat or Hair. .Name turns the Enum value into plain text.

gotchas: The Handle part must be named exactly `Handle`.
If the Attachment name in the Handle doesn't match any Attachment on the body, the accessory won't stay on.
Make the Handle not Anchored, or the character gets stuck.
AccessoryType is Unknown for accessories you add yourself, unless you set it.

Accessory.AccessoryType.simple: What kind of accessory this is, like Hat, Hair, Face, Back or Waist. It's Unknown unless the accessory came from the player's avatar or a HumanoidDescription, or you set it yourself.
Accessory.AccessoryType.example:
if accessory.AccessoryType == Enum.AccessoryType.Hat then
    print("It's a hat!")
end
